items.title: fix(fleet-dispatch): checked arithmetic on peer-declared chunk size in dechunked_len (#6512)
items.body: ## What `dechunked_len` (fleet-dispatch's chunked-response completeness checker) did raw arithmetic on the peer-declared chunk size: `size + 2` for the completeness guard and the slice index, `total += size` for the running total. For a chunk-size line naming `usize::MAX` or `usize::MAX - 1` that panics in debug builds and wraps in release builds, so the completeness verdict is computed from wrapped values (#6512; the #5579 rule — peer-declared sizes are never trusted). ## Fix Production code, not just the test: every arithmetic step on the declared size is now checked. - `size.checked_add(2)` — a size whose chunk + trailing CRLF cannot fit a `usize` reads as "not complete" (`None`). - The guard compares the buffered remainder against that checked end. - `total.checked_add(size)` — the running total is checked too. - The slice advances by the checked end. A chunk-size line that cannot describe a body within the buffered remainder is therefore "not complete" in every profile — never a panic, never a completed body computed from wrapped values. Signature and caller contract unchanged; `dechunk` (already guarded) untouched. ## Test The characterization test salvaged from PR #7524 pinned the old overflow-panic ("must overflow-panic on usize::MAX until #6512 lands") and failed deterministically in the release-profile Nix check phase, blocking every generation build from `main`. It is updated deliberately, as its own comment instructed, into `dechunked_len_huge_chunk_size_is_not_complete`, pinning: - both overflow sizes (`usize::MAX`, `usize::MAX - 1`) → `None` via direct calls (a panic would fail the test); - a huge declared size after a valid first chunk → `None`; - a large-but-plausible size (16 MiB) with insufficient bytes buffered → `None`; - the existing happy-path pins unchanged. Verified on the laptop, real crate: - `cargo test -p fleet-dispatch` (debug): 11 passed, 0 failed - `cargo test --release -p fleet-dispatch` (release): 11 passed, 0 failed Fixes #6512. This also unblocks the #7991 deploy: fork PR opencode#2237 and pin bump #8067 are merged, but no generation could build from `main` while this check-phase failure stood. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(fleet-dispatch): refuse invalid or truncated response framing (#8433)
items.body: Closes #8433. ## Problem `read_response` in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-dispatch/src/lib.rs` accepted invalid or truncated HTTP response framing: a malformed `Content-Length` was silently treated as absent (`value.parse().ok()`), duplicate lengths overwrote each other, `Transfer-Encoding` was accepted on a `contains("chunked")` test, EOF ended the body loop for every framing shape (so a body cut short of its declared length — or cut inside a chunked stream — was returned as if complete; a partial body can be valid JSON, making the truncation silent), and `dechunk` tolerated chunks missing their CRLF terminator. This conflicts with #6582's present-but-invalid refusal contract. ## Change Strict framing, validated where it is read: - **Headers:** every Content-Length statement (repeated headers, comma-joined values) must parse and all must agree — malformed or conflicting values are transport errors. Content-Length together with any Transfer-Encoding is refused as conflicting framing. Transfer-Encoding is accepted only as the single coding `chunked`; anything else (including `gzip, chunked`) is refused as unsupported. - **Body:** the reader now tracks an explicit `Framing` (length / chunked / close-delimited). EOF before a declared length is met, or anywhere inside a chunked stream (including its trailer section), is a truncation transport error naming the framing and the byte counts. Unframed bodies still run to connection close. - **Chunks:** one strict decoder (`parse_chunked`) distinguishes complete / incomplete / malformed: non-hex size lines and chunks missing their CRLF terminator are errors, never silent stops. The #6512 checked-arithmetic discipline is preserved (peer-declared sizes are checked before any slicing or allocation; the 64 MiB body bound still applies and the decoded body never exceeds the wire bytes). `dechunk`/`dechunked_len` are now wrappers over the strict parser. ## Verification - `cargo test -p fleet-dispatch` — 16 passed, 0 failed, including 5 new tests: loopback (`TcpListener`) round-trips for length/chunked-with-trailer/agreeing-duplicate/unframed bodies; refusal of malformed, conflicting, and CL+TE framings and unsupported codings; refusal of truncation after valid JSON bytes and of mid-chunk/mid-size-line cuts; refusal of malformed chunk sizes and missing CRLF terminators; trailer-section completeness pins. The pre-existing #6512 huge-chunk-size pins still pass. - `cargo fmt -p fleet-dispatch` applied. Queue task 14827 (repo-health-code-pilot, lane code-h) — triaged inline and fixed in the same claim. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: test(id-core): state the registry/catalog consistency pins against the production catalog under test-provider
items.body: ## What `cargo test --lib` at the `pkgs/id` workspace root — the Nix check phase's invocation (`pkgs/id/default.nix`) — fails deterministically on `main`: ``` world_caps::tests::test_provider_registry_matches_the_legacy_catalog_and_carries_manifests assertion `left == right` failed: legacy catalog derives from manifests left: [...20 production names..., "RegistryProbe"] right: [...20 production names...] ``` ## Mechanism #1061 (2950c3ffde, landed via #8031 after the generation-549 build) added the `RegistryProbe` provider behind id-core's `test-provider` feature, enabled **only** through the root package's dev-dependencies for the exit proof in `pkgs/id/tests/provider_registry_exit_proof.rs`. Cargo feature unification compiles id-core's lib test binary with the feature ON in workspace test builds, so the registry legitimately carries the probe — while this consistency test's expectations (registry == `CATALOG`, the 20-name list, entry count 20, default ceiling == catalog minus loc.*) are production-shape assertions written for the feature-off shape. The exit proof itself pins the complementary facts (probe absent from `CATALOG`, absent from every default ceiling). ## Fix (test-only, no production code) In `test_provider_registry_matches_the_legacy_catalog_and_carries_manifests`: - production expectations are stated against the registry names with the probe removed under `#[cfg(feature = "test-provider")]` — identical assertions, identical strength in the production shape; - the entry-count assertion becomes `production + EXTRA_CATALOG_ENTRIES.len()`, pinning that the only extras are the declared feature-gated ones; - the default-ceiling assertion subtracts the probe alongside loc.* under the feature, for the same #838 reason the exit proof expects it absent (its manifest default is Excluded). ## Evidence (laptop, real crate) - `cargo test -p id-core --lib`: **331 passed, 0 failed** - `cargo test -p id-core --lib --features test-utils,test-provider` (the unified shape that fails on main): **331 passed, 0 failed** - `rustfmt --check` on the touched file: clean. This is the third and last blocker for the #7991 deploy (after #6512 / PR #8069 and the mcpx refdoc regen / PR #8071): with it merged, a NixOS generation builds from `main` again and the opencode pin ff9858ae (#8067) can go live. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? ### Tokio broadcast channel calls clone in parallel, but does not require `Sync`
[GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The broadcast channel internally calls `clone` on the stored value when receiving it, and only requires `T:Send`. This means that using the broadcast channel with values that are `Send` but not `Sync` can trigger unsoundness if the `clone` implementation makes use of the value being `!Sync`.

Thank you to Austin Bonander for finding and reporting this issue.
